topics.title: Propositions and the converse of a proposition

concepts.learning_objective: State that a proposition is a statement that is either true or false.
Write the converse 'if Y then X' of a proposition of the form 'if X then Y'.
Recognise 'X implies Y' and 'Y when X' as other ways of saying 'if X then Y'.
Explain that a single counterexample is enough to show that a proposition is false.
Find counterexamples to claims that expressions such as Fermat numbers, 4n^2 + 1 or n^2 + n + 11 always give primes.

topics.title: Truth of a proposition compared with its converse

concepts.learning_objective: Show that a true proposition can have a false converse, using examples from numbers and daily life.
Give examples where a proposition and its converse are both true or both false.

topics.title: Perfect squares and an odd number of factors

concepts.learning_objective: Use factor-partner pairs to decide whether a number has an odd or an even number of factors.
Identify which of a proposition and its converse a chain of implications actually proves.

topics.title: Converses in geometry: the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem

concepts.learning_objective: State and apply the converse of the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem to decide whether a triangle is right-angled.
Judge the truth of converses of geometric propositions about lines and quadrilaterals.

topics.title: Divisibility and algebraic propositions and their converses

concepts.learning_objective: Decide whether converses of divisibility statements are true, giving counterexamples where needed.
Decide whether converses of statements such as 'if x = y then x^2 = y^2' are true for real numbers.
